A learner gains editor run/stop/save/Inspector/Remote-tree/Output habits; extends/func/_ready/_process/member variables/str()/$paths/:=; nodes built in code with .new() and add_child; mesh resource vs MeshInstance3D; StaticBody3D + CollisionShape3D kept independent of the visual; Vector3 components; local vs global position; b - a and .length(); per-frame re-reading; %-formatting. From Point_Trace on, 7 of the remaining 8 tutorials read excerpts of installed museum sources (arrays, loops, ImmediateMesh/SurfaceTool, ConvexPolygonShape3D, surface arrays, signals) without the learner writing anything. Portals is the exception: it offers typed pure helper functions (loops, Dictionary, Vector2, Basis inverse) with no harness to run them. Net: roughly Godot's 'first script' plus node/resource/collision basics, and vectors, practised. Arrays, loops, conditions and procedural meshes are only seen. sequences.godot_arc_today: WORKING TREE: the sequence opens with no code, because Descent's tutorial was rewritten into a 13-line prose spec (HEAD had 94 lines of gradient/momentum fragments). The remaining five halls are read-only fragments quoted from shipped code, with no runnable scaffold. A learner reading in order meets: Curve3D handles and arc-length sampling, instancing control points into an array, and parametric (u,v) surface formulas (Catenary). Then Verlet particles in parallel PackedVector3Arrays, iterative constraint loops, a const Dictionary of presets and ArrayMesh.add_surface_from_arrays (Relaxation). Then recursion returning {node, mass} dictionaries, const physical constants and a delta-phase scale animation (Equilibrium). Then an energy function, temperature-scaled random proposals, Metropolis acceptance, match on a cooling schedule and a stagnation counter (Annealing). Finally an array of part dictionaries, lerp toward a target, reading RigidBody3D velocities and a held-stillness timer as a win condition (Forge). The net gain is algorithmic plus some GDScript data structures. Godot-specific gains are Curve3D, ArrayMesh arrays and reading physics-body state. Every hall leans on unshown helpers (SBShapes, soft_body_sim, _cylinder_between, _sim, _rng).

sequences.godot_arc_today: All 8 tutorials are identical at HEAD and in the working tree (2026-04-24 cohort). They teach graph data structures in GDScript. There is a Graph class with a vertex Array, [a,b] edge pairs, degree and an adjacency Dictionary. Queues and stacks come from push_back, pop_front and pop_back. The algorithms are BFS, DFS and A* with came_from reconstruction, Brandes and power-iteration centralities, Tarjan and Kahn, union-find with a recursive find, Kruskal and Prim, Edmonds-Karp with Array-keyed Dictionaries, and Gale-Shapley. Godot content is thin: spheres tagged with set_meta, a _physics_process force layout that syncs visuals, Color.lerp heat colouring and await-animated edges. No hall runs as written. neighbours(), bfs_distances(), PriorityQueue, spawn_cylinder_between and COMPONENT_ROOM_SCENE are undefined; the Tarjan lambda would fail [inference]; the Hungarian algorithm is a stub. No spine tutorial mentions AStar3D, AStarGrid2D or any Navigation class, although this sequence's own impatient_river uses AStar3D.

DRIFT AGAINST ITS OWN RECORDS:
- The 2026-09-29-tutorial-lineage/DECISIONS.md still says 67 capability targets and 203 halls.
- The NOC comparison (claude-noc-vs-lineage-2026-09-29/README.md) measured 68 nodes and 167 edges. The file now has 71 and 171.
- The NOC review's structural findings are not applied:
  - vector still requires field;
  - random still requires array, transform and loop; noise still requires wave;
  - there is still no carried-work field and no 'assumes';
  - motion still only says "identify the time step" (the 60 vs 90 Hz physics experiment is not moved there).
agreements_vs_proposal: ALREADY ANSWERED: proposal §9.2 asks for "a small curriculum manifest" at doc/book/tutorial_path.json. That file does not exist, but the manifest does: doc/book/tutorial-lineage/curriculum.json (71 nodes, requires/learn/make/transfer/borrow), plus tools/build_tutorial_lineage.py and the live /tutorial-lineage atlas (HTTP 200 on localhost:3003). All are untracked, so this is true in the working tree only; at HEAD there is no manifest.

ALREADY ANSWERED: proposal §9.3 wants to prove one vertical chain before expanding. This matches TUTORIAL_LINEAGE l.79 ("better model... than expanding every tutorial at once"), curriculum priority [pickup, line-grid, trace-list] and PRIMITIVES_LINEAGE l.66-69.
ALREADY ANSWERED: 'Lists before the Array sequence' is STUDENT_TOOLBOX l.34, TUTORIAL_LINEAGE l.71 and curriculum issue trace-list.

ALREADY ANSWERED (working tree): 'Contact before a complete player' is done in the working-tree Point_One/tutorial.md and the untracked doc/book/studies/point-one kit: contact_probe.gd moves three pink feelers (tutorial l.7), per STUDENT_TOOLBOX l.31. The HEAD Point_One tutorial.md is the older axes-first text without it.

ALREADY ANSWERED: the proposal's 'Borrowing has a record' (operate / opened / change) parallels STUDENT_TOOLBOX l.13-17 (excerpt to inspect / step to build / part to borrow) and every node's borrow field. The axes differ: the proposal tracks learner state, the toolbox tracks what a text passage does. The proposal's three-level record is a real refinement the schema lacks.

PARTLY ANSWERED, and the proposal fills a documented gap: the §7 editorial contract overlaps TUTORIAL_LINEAGE's five questions (l.59-65) and the curriculum fields (Begins with ~ requires; Makes possible ~ make; New work ~ learn; Borrows ~ borrow; transfer ~ Check/independent change). 'Carry forward', 'Reuses', the exact starter/checkpoint and the expected 'Check' have no field. That is exactly what the NOC review found ("The schema has no field for what the student carries"; "borrow has no assumes beside it"). Both sides agree it must not become a prose checklist (STUDENT_TOOLBOX l.19; PRIMITIVES_LINEAGE l.62; proposal l.296).

PARTLY ANSWERED: the proposal's 'learner's continuing project' answers NOC lesson 3 (one carried object, the Mover / Ecosystem project, spans the book; a moving body does not span the lineage). The agreements carry one object (the point, the list, TraceData) but no personal project. TUTORIAL_LINEAGE l.9-11 'Follow one work as it becomes capable of more' is the closest ruling.

AGREES: three texts with distinct jobs. Point_Zero/intent.md l.20, STUDENT_TOOLBOX 'Read the encounter, then make' and forum 260929-ia2d6 'Three selections, one lineage' separate encounter and tutorial. The agreements' third selection is the HALL (placement), not technical.md, so the proposal's final/tutorial/technical triad is a different cut.

AGREES: 'some halls can remain contemplative' matches the reflect kind (6 nodes), TUTORIAL_LINEAGE l.33 and BOOK_FRAME l.16. Proposal §8 'no 204 compulsory lessons' matches 'not an equal lesson quota per hall' (README l.3).

AGREES: several later-sequence proposals match existing issue actions. Shader feedback 'if its supporting implementation is supplied' = shader-memory. Native ML example and zoom = network-zoom. Graph Theory 'open the route machinery used earlier' = graph-return. QFEP 'not a universal score' = proxy.borrow and qfep-drift. Randomness 'change its vocabulary or assignment, not only its seed' = random.transfer. The proposal does not mention the annealing bridge.
AGREES: 'keep historical descriptions from silently overriding current order' = README l.3. The proposal correctly treats ARC.md as older.
AGREES (verbatim echo): XR 'not an entrance examination' echoes day-zero.md l.42.

CONTRADICTS A RULING (Coordinates content): the proposal's opening table puts 'test proximity to a target', 'a Boolean condition' and 'a simple named input action' in Point Coordinates. The critique adds the target's condition-versus-event lesson there. Point_Coordinates/intent.md l.7 defers "Distance, arrow construction, label formatting and target state". TUTORIAL_LINEAGE l.47-49 rules "Distance belongs to the line". The Coordinates tutorial l.64 says we 'enjoy its falling response before calculating distance in Lines'.

CONTRADICTS A RULING (pickup): TUTORIAL_LINEAGE l.35-43 makes object-side pickup a Coordinates learning target, and curriculum coordinates requires xr (xr is upstream of 67/71 nodes). The proposal's opening table omits pickup entirely and moves XR to an 'overlapping route' where 'the first making route remains possible on an ordinary desktop'. The agreements do keep a desktop coordinate study, but the held point is the ruled next deliverable (issue pickup, severity next).

TENSION (Melencolia): the proposal makes Melencolia the first finished composition, with camera/light editing, an 'initial asset-import encounter' and a 'first distribution checkpoint' (export). The agreement gives Melencolia 'A reason to transform a relation, without a compulsory new coding mechanism' (TUTORIAL_LINEAGE l.31). curriculum geometry_return is kind reflect.

TENSION (Portals): the proposal's Portals studio teaches Button/Timer signals, reversing order and a staged process. Those controls exist in the hall (Primitives_Portals/final.md l.11, 31, 39, 47: NEXT RING, REVERSE, NEXT STEP, PLAY). The agreed capability is refinement: 'Follow a subdivision rule... A tolerance and the last displayed example have different meanings', with 'numerical error analysis can wait'. Different focus, not a direct contradiction.

TENSION (order of reusable scenes): the proposal saves the object as a scene in Polythedra. The agreement puts reusable scene vs mesh resource vs instances at the Cube shelf (instances node, hall Point_Animatedcube) and keeps Polythedra for enclosure vs collision (PRIMITIVES_LINEAGE l.32, l.44).

TENSION (player construction): the proposal builds CharacterBody3D, InputMap, Camera3D, Tween/AnimationPlayer and a scene transition in Transformation, aiming for a first playable work by the end of Transformation. The agreement borrows the player (transform.borrow 'Pickup base, player transport and safe reset'; scale.borrow 'Player scaling infrastructure') and returns to borrowed mechanisms 'when a later work needs to alter them' (TUTORIAL_LINEAGE l.43; STUDENT_TOOLBOX l.17). No curriculum node owns player, input, UI, save or export at all. That is a gap, not a ruling against the proposal.

CRITIQUE vs AGREEMENTS: #2 (build an ordinary scene without the supplied scene) runs against the current kit pattern, where every study inherits doc/book/studies/day-zero/base.tscn. No node covers scene.new_scene, but no ruling forbids it. #3 (events/signals exercise with a barrier) conflicts with the committed Point_Lines/tutorial.md l.56, which keeps the barrier, pickup, collision and reset machinery supplied: 'Implementing it is not a prerequisite for making our first segment'. #4 (lifetime in Arrays: remove a cube, keep its slot) is partly anticipated by array.transfer 'Remove an occupant without moving the other addresses' and the array_tutorial sequence question 'Does removing an occupant erase its address...'. #6 (particles missing) is true of both the proposal and curriculum.json.

CRITIQUE vs EXISTING TUTORIALS: #1's early programming progression is already largely in the committed Point_Zero/tutorial.md: names, values, assignment, func, indentation, retained member state, execution order ('Once, or repeatedly?'). Point_Lines covers local variables, calling a supplied function with arguments and a returned .length(). Defining one's own function with a return value is not taught anywhere in the opening yet.

NOT ADDRESSED BY THE PROPOSAL, KNOWN IN THE AGREEMENTS: the NOC-review time-step finding. XR Tools sets physics ticks to the headset refresh rate: 60 Hz desktop vs 90 Hz Quest, with per-tick damping measured at 0.451 vs 0.294 amplitude over 6 s. The proposal's Change row mentions step size but not the headset-dependent physics rate.

godot.project_setup:
Tag key: [D] = read this session in the Godot 4.6 docs. [K] = my own knowledge, not checked this session. [M] = measured in the repo on 2026-09-30, in the WORKING TREE unless it says HEAD. [I] = inference. Every doc path below is relative to https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.6/.

RENDERER [M]: project.godot sets no rendering/renderer/rendering_method. By [K] defaults that means Forward+ on the desktop and Mobile (Vulkan) on the Quest. [D] The 4.6 renderers page says Compatibility is "Recommended for standalone headsets" and Mobile for desktop headsets. deploying_to_android.html says "It is highly advisable to use the compatibility renderer (OpenGL)" on Android XR. [D] The Mobile renderer does not draw SDFGI, VoxelGI, SSIL, SSR, volumetric fog or TAA, and the docs table also lists SSAO as unsupported on Mobile. [M] Tracked .tscn/.tres/.gd files that turn these on: ssao 53, volumetric_fog 23, ssil 11, sdfgi 3, ssr 3; glow is on in 104. [I] So those looks drop out on the headset without any error. [M] commons/scenes/env.gd reads rendering_method and, for mobile_vr, forces bilinear scaling at 0.8.

XR [M]: xr/openxr/enabled=true, xr/shaders/enabled=true, foveation_level=3 with foveation_dynamic=true. [D] openxr_settings says foveation_level applies to the Compatibility renderer only; Mobile and Forward+ need Viewport.vrs_mode = VRS_XR. [M] No vrs_mode or VRS_XR appears anywhere in the repo's .gd/.tscn/.godot files. [I] So foveation is probably doing nothing on the Quest build. [M] Godot XR Tools is version 4.5.1 (addons/godot-xr-tools/plugin.cfg). It is enabled as an editor plugin together with map_tool_3d. XRToolsUserSettings and XRToolsRumbleManager are autoloads. [M] start_xr.gd sets Engine.physics_ticks_per_second from the headset refresh rate (reported rate × physics_rate_multiplier), so physics does not run at the project default of 60 Hz in XR. The main scene is res://commons/scenes/vr_staging.tscn, an XR Tools staging scene; for desktop there is a separate desktop rig. openxr_action_map.tres is tracked.

PHYSICS [M]: 3d/physics_engine="GodotPhysics3D" is set explicitly, with contact_max_allowed_penetration=0.001. [D] Godot 4.6 makes Jolt the default for NEW 3D projects (4.6 release notes and using_jolt_physics). A learner's fresh project will therefore run Jolt, not what the course project runs. Known differences: joint parameters, single-body joint frames, kinematic contacts, SoftBody3D×Area3D, ray face_index. [M] There are 12 named 3D physics layers, 1–5 and 17–23 (Static World … UI Objects); [K] this is XR Tools' layer scheme.

AUTOLOADS [M]: 27 in the working tree. HEAD has 26; LeakData is the uncommitted addition, and it is the only difference between project.godot and HEAD. INPUT [M]: The InputMap holds move_forward/backward/left/right, jump, interact, fly, action_sprint, action_crouch, vr_button_a and toggle_artifact_catalog. gui/common/drop_mouse_on_gui_input_disabled=true. The audio input driver is enabled. File logging is on (12 files). Import: blender import is disabled and import_etc2_astc=true.

EXPORT [M]: There are only two presets. (1) Android "adaresearchonexy": gradle build, arm64-v8a only, xr_mode=1 (OpenXR), Meta plugin, Quest 2/3/Pro, shader_baker disabled, include_filter *.md,*.json, excluding tools/, doc/, ada_run/** and commons/testing. The android/ template is 4.6.stable, and android/build/config.gradle names openxrVendorsVersion 4.2.2-stable. (2) Web. There is no Windows desktop preset.

TRACKING [M]: .gitignore ignores /addons/* (except audio_catalog_editor, map_sequence_editor and element_editor), /android/ and /assets/. XR Tools is on disk but untracked; only user_settings.gd is tracked, yet 200 tracked .gd/.tscn files reference res://addons/godot-xr-tools. A fresh clone is therefore not a complete, runnable project. doc/book/day-zero.md and STUDENT_TOOLBOX.md are untracked (working tree only). Day Zero points at a separate small desktop base (project.godot + base.tscn: fixed camera, light, floor, environment, a "Hello, world" label, no player, no XR). Point_Coordinates/ is untracked.

API USAGE [M]: One pass over 9,858 files: .gd 5,777, .tscn 3,704, .tres 73, .gdshader 304. Excluded: addons, doc, ada_run, android, .godot, .claude. Raw counts are in scratchpad/godotpath/api_usage_counts.txt, produced by api_usage.py.

godot.official_order:
GODOT'S OWN ORDER [D, read this session]:

1. Getting Started > Introduction. Introduction to Godot, then Learn to Code with GDScript, then key concepts, then a first look at the editor, then learning new features, then design philosophy. Learn to Code sends non-programmers out to the external "Learn GDScript From Zero" app.

2. Step by step. Six pages, all taught with 2D nodes.
   - Nodes and Scenes: a Label, the Scene dock, the Inspector, Run Current Scene vs Run Project, setting the main scene, saving .tscn, res://.
   - Creating instances: a ball RigidBody2D scene, instancing, per-instance overrides with a revert button, and "make resources unique before editing".
   - Scripting languages.
   - Creating your first script: Sprite2D, extends, _init, member variables, _process(delta), rotation, position with Vector2.UP.rotated. It states "we assume you have programming foundations".
   - Listening to player input: the Input singleton (is_action_pressed) vs _unhandled_input, the built-in ui_* actions, delta.
   - Using signals: Button.pressed connected in the editor, set_process(not is_processing()), a Timer connected in code in _ready, declaring a custom signal, then signal arguments with .emit().

3. Your first 2D game. Seven parts. The docs recommend it before 3D because 3D "tend[s] to be more complicated".

4. Your first 3D game. Its stated prerequisite is the full getting-started series.
   - 01: import the starter project; a Main Node; Ground as StaticBody3D with a CollisionShape3D (BoxShape3D) and a MeshInstance3D (BoxMesh) at 60×2×60, y=-1; grid snapping (Y); DirectionalLight3D with shadows.
   - 02: a CharacterBody3D, then a Pivot Node3D, then a .glb model dragged in from the FileSystem; SphereShape3D; five InputMap actions bound to keyboard and joypad.
   - 03: _physics_process, Input.is_action_pressed, direction.normalized(), Basis.looking_at, gravity when not is_on_floor, velocity + move_and_slide, @export speed; an orthographic Camera3D on a Marker3D pivot (shadow quality depends on Far).
   - 04: the mob as a CharacterBody3D; VisibleOnScreenNotifier3D.screen_exited then queue_free; look_at_from_position, rotate_y, randf_range, rotated.
   - 05: @export PackedScene; Path3D with PathFollow3D.progress_ratio; Timer.timeout; instantiate + add_child; randf.
   - 06: named physics layers and masks; groups; get_slide_collision in a for-range loop; the collision normal dotted with UP; a custom signal "squashed"; a bounce impulse.
   - 07: an Area3D hitbox with body_entered; a hit signal connected across scenes; queue_free; stopping the Timer.
   - 08: Label, a Theme and font, anchors, a ColorRect overlay, .connect with a callable plus bind, _unhandled_input with ui_accept, get_tree().reload_current_scene(), AudioStreamPlayer music as an autoload.
   - 09: AnimationPlayer tracks and keyframes, easing, autoplay and loop, speed_scale from code, reusing the animation on the mob.
   - Going further: Scripting, then 3D and Physics, then Inputs.

The manual beyond this is organised by subsystem, not by order: 3D (intro, transforms, procedural geometry, 3D text, materials, lights, particles, environment, MultiMesh/LOD/occlusion, CSG, GridMap, spring arm), physics (14 pages), animation (7), audio (6), shaders (12), UI, navigation (18), I/O (5), performance (10), export (15), XR (16, including 2 XR Tools pages).

WHAT THE OFFICIAL PATH NEVER TEACHES: procedural meshes, shaders, save files, export/builds, version control, profiling, custom Resources, threads, XR. Export is documented only in the manual.

HOW ADA DIFFERS [I]:
- Ada opens in 3D and skips 2D. So the official step-by-step can serve as side reading, but its screenshots won't match.
- Ada must teach programming itself, because the docs assume it. Point Zero's _ready/_process is the equivalent of docs step 4.
- Ada meets instancing and signals much later than the docs, which put both in steps 2 and 6.
- The first 3D game reaches a complete loop in 9 parts: player, enemy, spawn, collide, score, retry, animate. Nothing in the Primitives sequence yet includes a player, a retry or an export.

capabilities.use: Imports a project in the Project Manager, opens a scene, uses Run Project (F5) vs Run Current Scene (F6), stops the game and saves.
capabilities.understand: project.godot holds the settings and the main scene; res:// is the project root; a .tscn is one file inside a project; .godot/ is a cache that can be regenerated.
capabilities.change: Sets the main scene and adds an input action or autoload in Project Settings; moves files inside the FileSystem dock without breaking res:// or uid links.
capabilities.caution: [M] The course project starts vr_staging.tscn and has 27 autoloads in the working tree (26 at HEAD). It holds 9,858 script/scene files, so it is not a first project. Day Zero (doc/book/day-zero.md, untracked) supplies a separate small desktop base; keep Day Zero on it. [K] Moving files in the OS file browser breaks references.

capabilities.use: Adds, renames and reparents nodes in the Scene dock, and edits the selected node in the Inspector.
capabilities.understand: A scene is a tree with one root. The Inspector groups properties by inherited class, and a revert arrow marks an override.
capabilities.change: Restructures a scene (reparents, changes a node's type, saves a branch as its own scene) and keeps its scripts and references working.
capabilities.caution: [D] The official step-by-step teaches this with 2D nodes: adding a Label switches the editor to 2D. Ada's base is 3D, so the docs' screenshots won't match. [M] visible=false hides every descendant (CLAUDE.md); to hide a single mesh, set layers = 0.

capabilities.use: Orbits, pans and zooms; flies with right mouse + WASD; frames the selection (F); moves, rotates and scales with gizmos; toggles snapping (Y).
capabilities.understand: Local vs global gizmo space, snap steps, orthographic views, and that the editor's preview sun and environment are not in the running scene.
capabilities.change: Sets snap increments and multi-view layouts, and places objects precisely by typing transform values.
capabilities.caution: [K] A scene can look lit in the editor and run dark. [M] Ada halls are authored as JSON grids (map_data.json, the map-builder), not placed in the viewport, so the museum offers little viewport-placement practice. The learner's own scenes have to supply it.

capabilities.use: Runs and stops the game, reads print() and errors in Output/Debugger, and clicks through from an error to its line.
capabilities.understand: Errors vs warnings, stack traces, the Remote scene tree and Inspector showing the live game, breakpoints and stepping.
capabilities.change: Uses breakpoints and push_warning, edits live values through Remote, and runs from the command line to read logs.
capabilities.caution: [M] File logging is on. Many faults here show only in the log: SHADER ERROR at first draw, 'Error calling from signal' when a handler's argument count is wrong, and Quest loader failures (read with adb logcat). Point_Lines/tutorial.md already uses the Remote inspector. Headless runs print output but draw nothing.

capabilities.use: Commits a known working state and returns to it.
capabilities.understand: What to track (.tscn, .gd, .tres, project.godot, .uid) vs what to regenerate (.godot/), and that large binaries need care.
capabilities.change: Branches, reads a .tscn diff, resolves a scene conflict, and writes a .gitignore that still gives a clone that opens.
capabilities.caution: [M] /addons/*, /android/ and /assets/ are gitignored. XR Tools 4.5.1 is untracked, yet 200 tracked files reference it, so a clone or worktree loads maps with zero artifacts and no error. Several agents share this one working tree, so never use git stash. [D] The official getting-started path does not teach version control.

capabilities.use: Declares a var, assigns to it, prints it, and writes arithmetic and string expressions.
capabilities.understand: Member vs local scope; value types (int, float, bool, String, Vector3); integer division; = vs ==.
capabilities.change: Names state clearly and replaces magic numbers with named members.
capabilities.caution: [D] The docs assume 'programming foundations' and send beginners to the external 'Learn GDScript From Zero' app, so Point Zero has to teach this itself. [M] Point_Zero/tutorial.md (88 lines) introduces _ready, _process and position.

capabilities.use: Calls engine methods and its own functions with arguments, and writes a func that returns a value.
capabilities.understand: Parameters vs arguments, return values, local vs member state, and that engine callbacks are functions the engine calls.
capabilities.change: Pulls repeated code into pure helper functions with deliberate signatures.
capabilities.caution: [M] The Primitives_Portals tutorial defines helpers (torus_counts, through_portal, polygon_perimeter). Pure functions are what the repo's headless probes can check.

capabilities.use: Puts setup in _ready, per-frame work in _process(delta) and physics in _physics_process(delta).
capabilities.understand: Children are ready before their parent; the drawn frame vs the fixed physics tick; delta makes rates independent of frame rate.
capabilities.change: Picks the right callback, toggles processing with set_process, and sets process priority.
capabilities.caution: [M] The physics tick is 60 Hz on desktop, but XR Tools sets it to the headset refresh. Headless Godot never increments frames_drawn. The museum lane calls apply_grid_config BEFORE _ready, so an artifact must build once, in _ready, behind a _built guard.

capabilities.use: Writes if/elif/else with comparisons and and/or/not.
capabilities.understand: bool as a value; a state ('inside') vs an event ('just entered'); match.
capabilities.change: Replaces tangles of flags with enum + match, and detects edges (was vs is).
capabilities.caution: [I] The target in Point_Coordinates (the critique's condition-vs-event example) is the natural teaching case. Area3D enter/exit is the engine's built-in form of an event.

capabilities.use: Writes for i in range(n), for item in array, and a while loop with a guard.
capabilities.understand: Bounds and off-by-one errors; a long loop blocks its whole frame.
capabilities.change: Spreads a heavy loop across frames, and uses break/continue on purpose.
capabilities.caution: [D] The first 3D game has one loop: for index in range(get_slide_collision_count()). [M] 'for' is the most frequent construct in the Primitives tutorials.

capabilities.use: Creates an array, appends, indexes, calls size(), iterates and removes.
capabilities.understand: Arrays are shared by reference; duplicate() vs deep copy; removing while iterating; empty and out-of-bounds cases.
capabilities.change: Chooses between Array, typed Array[T] and Packed arrays, and keeps data separate from nodes.
capabilities.caution: [M] 2,006 files use typed Array[..]. Point_Trace brings in append before the Arrays sequence, which is the proposal's 'lists before arrays' accommodation.

capabilities.use: Creates a Dictionary, reads with get(key, default), sets values and iterates the keys.
capabilities.understand: Reference semantics; the keys 1 and 1.0 are different; insertion order is kept.
capabilities.change: Designs a record schema and converts it to and from JSON or a Resource.
capabilities.caution: [M] Ada's content chain is JSON. JSON parses every number as a float (2 arrives as 2.0), String() on a JSON number throws (use str()), and editor-authored map cells are strings.

capabilities.use: Fills a PackedVector3Array or PackedInt32Array and passes it to mesh or MultiMesh APIs.
capabilities.understand: Packed arrays copy on assignment, are contiguous and fast, and are the format the mesh APIs expect.
capabilities.change: Builds mesh arrays directly and chooses Packed over Array when speed matters.
capabilities.caution: [M] 1,147 files use them. [K] Changing a packed array you got from a property only changes a copy, so assign it back.

capabilities.use: Joins strings, formats with % and str(), and prints readouts.
capabilities.understand: String vs StringName vs NodePath; format specifiers; split and strip.
capabilities.change: Writes a small parser (L-system rules, map tokens).
capabilities.caution: [M] GDScript has no %e format (project memory). The map token grammar 'artifact:rotation:y_offset' and the '#key:number' config shorthand are real parsing cases in this repo; the shorthand was once misread as a rotation.

capabilities.use: Annotates var x: int, func f(a: Vector3) -> float, and uses :=.
capabilities.understand: Types catch mistakes when the script is parsed and speed up code; Variant; casting with 'as'; typed arrays.
capabilities.change: Turns on typing warnings, adds types to an untyped script and designs typed interfaces.
capabilities.caution: [M] Object.set() with a wrong-typed value on a typed property is refused with no error or warning. This caused the false DNA 'tier' verdict. Read assignments back.

capabilities.use: Extends a node type and uses a class_name as a type.
capabilities.understand: Inheritance; class_name as a global name; inner classes; composing child nodes vs inheriting.
capabilities.change: Pulls out a base class or a reusable component node.
capabilities.caution: [M] 2,568 files declare a class_name. A .gd snapshot kept under doc/ declares its class twice (tools/check_global_classes.py catches this). On Quest, a threaded load failed to resolve a class_name base and cached the script as broken; the fix is _XR_CLASS_WARMER in vrStaging.gd. const Skin := preload() hides a built-in class.

capabilities.use: Uses @export to tune a value in the Inspector, and @onready var x = $Child.
capabilities.understand: Exported values are saved per instance in the .tscn; @onready runs just before _ready; export hints (range, enum, file).
capabilities.change: Designs an artifact's Inspector surface, with setters that rebuild and export groups.
capabilities.caution: [M] 2,821 files use @export. Changing a default is dangerous: some artifacts have up to 1,077 live placements. An @export_enum String property given an int value is silently refused. The proposal places this at Primitives_Ignorance.

capabilities.use: Connects a built-in signal (Button.pressed, Timer.timeout, body_entered) in the editor or with .connect().
capabilities.understand: Declaring signal x(arg), emit(), that the handler's argument count must match, bind(); who detects vs who responds.
capabilities.change: Designs signal interfaces between scenes, disconnects in _exit_tree, and replaces polling with signals.
capabilities.caution: [M] A signal with one argument connected to a method with none fails on every emit; the button is dead and only the log says why. call_group() reaches every hall the museum has streamed in. 1,217 files call .connect.

capabilities.use: Awaits get_tree().create_timer(t).timeout or any signal, and uses a Timer node.
capabilities.understand: A function with await becomes a coroutine and returns to its caller; the node can be freed before it resumes.
capabilities.change: Sequences a staged reveal or step process with awaits and cancellation checks.
capabilities.caution: [M] 1,208 files use await. Config can arrive before the node is in the tree; guard with await tree_entered. [K] After an await, check is_inside_tree().

capabilities.use: Checks for null and is_instance_valid, and reads and fixes an error.
capabilities.understand: assert only runs in debug builds; push_error and push_warning; a freed object is not null; failing loudly vs falling back.
capabilities.change: Handles bad input (a missing file, broken JSON) with a named fallback.
capabilities.caution: [M] 758 files call push_error/warning, 1,306 use is_instance_valid, and only 27 use assert. The common failure here is a silent fallback: materials after a SHADER ERROR, artifacts reverting to defaults.

capabilities.use: Calls a recursive function with a depth parameter.
capabilities.understand: Base case, stack depth, exponential growth, and explicit stacks as the alternative.
capabilities.change: Rewrites a recursion as an explicit stack or queue with a work budget.
capabilities.caution: [I] Taught in the Fractals and L-Systems halls. A deep recursion in _ready stalls a headset frame, so pair it with perf.budget.

capabilities.use: Uses const, enum State {...} and static func.
capabilities.understand: Named constants; enums are ints underneath; static functions carry no instance state.
capabilities.change: Models explicit states (closed / opening / open / closing) with an enum and match.
capabilities.caution: [M] 674 files declare static func and 266 declare an enum. The critique's barrier exercise needs this, but not a state-machine framework.

capabilities.use: Gives a MeshInstance3D a Mesh and a Material in the Inspector.
capabilities.understand: Nodes act in the tree; Resources are data (mesh, material, shape, texture) that nodes reference and can share.
capabilities.change: Saves a resource to .tres, reuses it, and swaps it at runtime.
capabilities.caution: [M] Point_One/tutorial.md names MeshInstance3D, StaticBody3D and CollisionShape3D, which makes it the natural place for this distinction.

capabilities.use: Creates a scene with a root and children, saves the .tscn and runs it with F6.
capabilities.understand: Choosing the root type; a saved scene is a reusable template; editable children.
capabilities.change: Splits a large scene into sub-scenes with 'Save Branch as Scene'.
capabilities.caution: [I] The critique is right that Ada's tutorials build mostly in code (loops, SurfaceTool). An explicit exercise building a scene by hand must come before leaving Primitives.

capabilities.use: Drags a .tscn into another scene; in code, @export var s: PackedScene, then s.instantiate() and add_child().
capabilities.understand: Template vs instance, per-instance overrides, editable children, the cost of instantiating.
capabilities.change: Builds a spawner or pool and nests scenes on purpose.
capabilities.caution: [M] 1,228 files call instantiate(). The Ada grid instances artifacts by registry token and configures the ROOT through apply_grid_config; a root without a script silently ignores its config.

capabilities.use: Hides and shows, remove_child, and queue_free.
capabilities.understand: Hide vs remove from the tree vs free; a freed object leaves stale references; a node outside the tree does not process.
capabilities.change: Keeps the data slot when a node goes, rebuilds from data, and pools instead of freeing.
capabilities.caution: [M] 2,801 files call queue_free and 1,306 use is_instance_valid, so lifetime is a daily concern here. Hiding propagates to descendants.

capabilities.use: Uses change_scene_to_file and reload_current_scene for a retry.
capabilities.understand: What a scene change destroys, what survives (autoloads), and current_scene.
capabilities.change: Writes a loader that swaps a child scene and carries a record across; threaded loading with progress.
capabilities.caution: [M] Under XR Tools staging, reload_current_scene() reloads vr_staging.tscn, which is the menu; maps load through staging.load_scene. The first 3D game's retry pattern does not carry over to the museum.

capabilities.use: Uses $Child and get_node(), add_to_group and is_in_group, and %UniqueName.
capabilities.understand: NodePaths break when the tree changes; groups are tags; group calls reach the whole tree.
capabilities.change: Replaces brittle paths with exported NodePaths, unique names or signals.
capabilities.caution: [M] 447 files use groups. In the museum, call_group reaches other streamed-in halls.

capabilities.use: Registers an autoload and calls it by name.
capabilities.understand: Autoloads live above current_scene and survive scene changes; they couple everything to global state.
capabilities.change: Decides what really must outlive a scene, and replaces a global with a passed reference or a Resource.
capabilities.caution: [M] A learner who opens the course project inherits all 27 autoloads. A --script SceneTree probe cannot name an autoload at compile time, though it can reach it by path at runtime. The proposal advises against an all-purpose autoload.

capabilities.use: Uses Make Unique, resource_local_to_scene or duplicate() before editing a material on one instance.
capabilities.understand: Resources are shared by reference, so editing one edits every user.
capabilities.change: Chooses sharing on purpose (one palette material) vs per-instance copies.
capabilities.caution: [D] The instancing page itself warns about this. [M] 719 files call duplicate(). The proposal gives this to the Color sequence.

capabilities.use: Writes extends Resource with a class_name and @export fields, and saves a .tres.
capabilities.understand: Only exported properties serialize; load() caches; a .tres from outside can run scripts.
capabilities.change: Models presets and recipes as validated custom Resources.
capabilities.caution: [M] Only 22 files extend Resource; Ada keeps its recipes in JSON registries and maps. There is little in the project to borrow for this.

capabilities.use: Reads and writes position, adds and subtracts vectors, and uses length(), normalized() and distance_to().
capabilities.understand: Points vs directions; dot for facing and angle; cross for perpendiculars and normals; units are metres.
capabilities.change: Derives steering, projections and reflections from vector algebra.
capabilities.caution: [M] The Point_Coordinates tutorial (untracked, working tree) and Point_Lines teach position, subtraction and length. [D] The first 3D game uses a dot product with the collision normal to detect a stomp.

capabilities.use: Uses position vs global_position, parent/child nesting, to_local and to_global.
capabilities.understand: Transform3D is a Basis plus an origin; transforms compose down the hierarchy; scale lives in the basis.
capabilities.change: Computes transforms directly and converts between frames.
capabilities.caution: [M] 2,243 files use Transform3D. In XR everything is relative to XROrigin3D. The museum places segments at world z = -4 with the grid starting at x = -1 (project memory), so frames matter.

capabilities.use: Uses rotate_y, rotation_degrees, look_at and a pivot Node3D.
capabilities.understand: Euler order and gimbal lock; Basis vs Quaternion; look_at faces -Z and fails when the target is parallel to up.
capabilities.change: Slerps between orientations with Quaternion and builds a basis from axes.
capabilities.caution: [D] The first 3D game uses a pivot, Basis.looking_at, look_at_from_position and rotate_y. [M] 667 files use look_at and 53 use Quaternion. Quaternions can wait.

capabilities.use: Uses lerp and move_toward scaled by delta, and ease().
capabilities.understand: Smoothing that is independent of frame rate (1 - exp(-k*delta)) vs a fixed lerp every frame; easing curves.
capabilities.change: Writes custom easing or spring motion and interpolates transforms.
capabilities.caution: [M] 1,350 files use lerp. [K] lerp(a, b, 0.1) every frame behaves differently at 60 Hz on desktop and 72/90 Hz on the headset.

capabilities.use: Puts a BoxMesh, SphereMesh or CylinderMesh on a MeshInstance3D and sets its sizes.
capabilities.understand: A PrimitiveMesh is a Resource generated from parameters; the visible mesh is not the collision shape.
capabilities.change: Blocks out a level from primitives with matching shapes, or generates them in code.
capabilities.caution: [M] 2,946 files use primitive meshes; they are the house style.

capabilities.use: Builds a triangle with SurfaceTool (begin, add_vertex, commit), or lines with ImmediateMesh.
capabilities.understand: Winding order (Godot front faces are clockwise), normals, UVs, indices, surfaces, ArrayMesh arrays.
capabilities.change: Writes a mesher (grid, extrusion, marching cubes) with correct normals and collision built from the same data.
capabilities.caution: [M] Central to Ada's spine: SurfaceTool 428 files, ArrayMesh 506, ImmediateMesh 372. SurfaceTool computes normals as (a-c)x(a-b), so a mesher wound the textbook way comes out inside out with nothing visibly wrong. For a general 3D developer this is a branch, not core.

capabilities.use: Sets up a MultiMeshInstance3D with instance_count and set_instance_transform.
capabilities.understand: Many copies in one draw call; per-instance colour and custom data; no per-instance collision or picking.
capabilities.change: Replaces thousands of MeshInstance3D nodes and animates instances in a shader.
capabilities.caution: [M] 575 files. Headless keeps no MultiMesh data (transforms read back as identity). The capture AABB counts only MeshInstance3D, so a MultiMesh artifact needs a layers = 0 anchor mesh.

capabilities.use: Combines CSG shapes with union, subtract and intersect, and turns on use_collision.
capabilities.understand: The docs call CSG 'intended for prototyping'; operand order matters; rebuilding at runtime is costly.
capabilities.change: Bakes a CSG blockout to a mesh and chooses its collision separately.
capabilities.caution: [M] 313 files. The museum's walk map cannot see CSG collision; GT_Foundations was sealed at both doors because of it (project memory).

capabilities.use: Paints a GridMap from a MeshLibrary.
capabilities.understand: Each MeshLibrary item carries a mesh, collision and navmesh; cell size and orientation.
capabilities.change: Builds a MeshLibrary from a scene and fills a GridMap from data.
capabilities.caution: [M] Only 2 files use GridMap. Ada's own 3-layer JSON grid (commons/grid/GridSystem.gd) does this job instead. Teach them as two different implementations, as the proposal does.

capabilities.use: Sets albedo, metallic, roughness, emission and transparency on a StandardMaterial3D.
capabilities.understand: PBR parameters, unshaded mode, the cost of transparency and its sorting, cull mode, override vs surface material.
capabilities.change: Builds a small material library and drives material properties from code.
capabilities.caution: [M] 3,136 files. Emission cannot make a black body glow, and in UNSHADED mode it is added after alpha. An emission_texture that is assigned but not yet bound samples as WHITE. [D] Transparent objects sort by node position, not per vertex.

capabilities.use: Assigns an imported image as albedo_texture, and makes an ImageTexture from an Image in code.
capabilities.understand: UVs; import settings (compression, mipmaps, filter, repeat); mobile limit of 4096, and power-of-two sizes for repeating textures.
capabilities.change: Generates textures procedurally and updates them efficiently.
capabilities.caution: [M] import_etc2_astc=true is set, which Android needs. 203 files use ImageTexture and 177 Image.create. [K] Re-uploading a texture every frame is expensive on Quest.

capabilities.use: Adds a DirectionalLight3D with shadows and a WorldEnvironment with sky and ambient light.
capabilities.understand: Light types and their cost, shadows, ambient vs direct, tonemapping, fog, and which effects each renderer supports.
capabilities.change: Lights for mood and legibility, bakes LightmapGI, and budgets lights per mesh.
capabilities.caution: [M] The Quest runs the Mobile renderer here. [D] Mobile does not render SSAO, SSIL, SSR, SDFGI or volumetric fog. [M] Tracked files enable ssao 53, volumetric_fog 23, ssil 11, sdfgi 3, ssr 3. [I] Those looks vanish on the headset. [D] Glow (104 files) turns off foveation under Compatibility. [K] The editor's preview sun is not in the game.

capabilities.use: Places a Camera3D, makes it current, and sets FOV, near and far.
capabilities.understand: Perspective vs orthographic; near/far and depth precision (z-fighting); which camera is current.
capabilities.change: Builds camera rigs (pivot, SpringArm3D, smoothing) and multiple viewports.
capabilities.caution: [M] 1,461 files mention Camera3D. An artifact's own camera, or the museum walker's camera guard, can take over the current camera and the audio listener. In XR the XRCamera3D is tracked, so code must not move it.

capabilities.use: Defines actions in the InputMap and uses Input.is_action_pressed, is_action_just_pressed and Input.get_vector.
capabilities.understand: Physical key vs named action; held vs just pressed; deadzones; keyboard and joypad on one action.
capabilities.change: Adds runtime remapping through the InputMap API and saves it.
capabilities.caution: [M] The InputMap has move_*, jump, interact, fly, sprint, crouch, vr_button_a and toggle_artifact_catalog. XR input goes through openxr_action_map.tres instead. Only 29 files call Input.is_action_*; most interaction arrives as XR Tools signals.

capabilities.use: Handles discrete presses in _unhandled_input(event) and captures the mouse for mouse-look.
capabilities.understand: Event order (_input, then GUI, then _unhandled_input); set_input_as_handled; mouse modes; relative mouse motion.
capabilities.change: Separates UI input from gameplay input, and builds a menu that consumes input.
capabilities.caution: [M] 309 files define _input vs 44 _unhandled_input. The desktop right-click carry never emits an XR pickable's picked_up/dropped; artifacts need the separate desktop hooks.

capabilities.use: Moves a CharacterBody3D with velocity, gravity, move_and_slide() and is_on_floor().
capabilities.understand: Direction relative to the camera basis; velocity vs position; floor, wall and slope parameters; why this runs in _physics_process.
capabilities.change: Adds jump, sprint, crouch and coyote time; first-person mouse-look; floor snapping.
capabilities.caution: [M] Ada's player is the XR Tools XROrigin/PlayerBody with movement providers, not a CharacterBody3D the learner writes. The Day Zero base has no player at all. A controller the learner builds would be new teaching material; 68 files call move_and_slide.

capabilities.use: Uses a Label, a Button (pressed) and an HSlider (value_changed) on a CanvasLayer.
capabilities.understand: Control coordinates vs Node3D coordinates; controls report through signals; focus.
capabilities.change: Builds a custom control, and routes one function from mouse, controller and test callers.
capabilities.caution: [M] In VR, Ada's controls are 3D artifacts (InteractableAreaButton, slider_horizontal.tscn emitting slider_moved), not Control nodes. 652 files use Controls, mostly desktop overlays.

capabilities.use: Uses anchor presets, VBox/HBox/Margin containers, and a Theme with a font.
capabilities.understand: Anchors and offsets vs layout by containers; size flags; focus neighbours; theme inheritance.
capabilities.change: Builds menus that resize, theme variations, and controller navigation.
capabilities.caution: [M] set_anchors_preset keeps the current rect, so a freshly made Control stays 0x0 and draws nothing while its numbers look right.

capabilities.use: Uses Label3D (billboard, font size, pixel size), and a SubViewport that shows a Control on a quad.
capabilities.understand: Pixel size vs world units; billboarding; the render cost of a SubViewport; pointing at 3D panels.
capabilities.change: Builds an interactive 3D panel (XR Tools Viewport2Din3D or its own raycast).
capabilities.caution: [M] Label3D is Ada's main text surface (1,659 files); 231 files use SubViewport. [K] Each SubViewport costs an extra render pass per eye in XR.

capabilities.use: Uses a StaticBody3D floor, a RigidBody3D prop, a CharacterBody3D player and an AnimatableBody3D platform.
capabilities.understand: Who moves each body (engine, code or animation); sleeping; freeze modes.
capabilities.change: Chooses body types for a design and converts between them.
capabilities.caution: [M] This project explicitly uses GodotPhysics3D. [D] A new 4.6 project defaults to Jolt, which differs in joint parameters, kinematic contacts and SoftBody×Area. The learner's project and the course project will behave slightly differently.

capabilities.use: Gives a body a CollisionShape3D and sets its layer and mask.
capabilities.understand: The layer says what a body is, the mask what it detects; primitive vs convex vs concave shapes and their costs.
capabilities.change: Designs a layer scheme, generates collision from meshes, and debugs with Visible Collision Shapes.
capabilities.caution: [M] Named layers 1–5 and 17–23 follow the XR Tools scheme [K]. A learner's object must sit on these layers for pickup and pointer to work. [K] A concave (trimesh) shape cannot be used on a moving RigidBody.

capabilities.use: Uses an Area3D with body_entered and body_exited as a trigger or pickup.
capabilities.understand: monitoring vs monitorable; enter/exit are events while get_overlapping_bodies is state; overlaps lag one frame.
capabilities.change: Builds zones (gravity, damping), hazard volumes and proximity triggers.
capabilities.caution: [M] Ada's hazards (h:fire, h:death), teleporters and museum walk-into triggers are Area3D, and the museum seals some walk-into triggers. [D] Under Jolt, SoftBody3D and Area3D do not interact.

capabilities.use: Uses a RayCast3D node, or intersect_ray from the camera.
capabilities.understand: Mask, exclude and collide_with_areas; queries belong in the physics step; shape casts.
capabilities.change: Builds picking, line of sight, ground probes and placement checks.
capabilities.caution: [M] 201 files. [D] Jolt returns face_index -1 unless it is enabled.

capabilities.use: Calls apply_central_impulse and apply_force, sets gravity_scale and a PhysicsMaterial, and adds a HingeJoint3D.
capabilities.understand: Force vs impulse; _integrate_forces; mass and damping; sleeping; joint limits.
capabilities.change: Builds a pendulum or vehicle and compares a hand-written integrator with the engine.
capabilities.caution: [M] Settling depends on the physics rate: a thrown die settled in 15 of 16 throws at 90 Hz but only 2 of 16 at 60 Hz. A fixed-interval sampler in _physics_process can fire at most once per step. Test at 60 and 90 Hz.

capabilities.use: Uses a SoftBody3D with a mesh and pinned points.
capabilities.understand: Simulation precision, pressure, pinning, and the cost of mesh resolution.
capabilities.change: Tunes cloth or jelly and couples it with rigid bodies.
capabilities.caution: [M] 65 files (the Soft Bodies sequence). [D] Under Jolt there is no SoftBody3D–Area3D interaction. [K] Soft bodies are heavy on the Quest CPU.

capabilities.use: Calls create_tween().tween_property(node, 'position', target, 0.5).
capabilities.understand: A Tween is bound to its node; parallel vs chained steps; easing; kill().
capabilities.change: Sequences feedback animations and replaces hand-written lerps.
capabilities.caution: [M] 283 files; Tween is the project's main animation tool.

capabilities.use: Keyframes position and rotation in an AnimationPlayer, and uses play(), autoplay and loop.
capabilities.understand: Property, method and audio tracks; easing per key; the RESET track; speed_scale.
capabilities.change: Calls methods from tracks, blends clips, and reuses animations across scenes.
capabilities.caution: [M] Only 20 files use AnimationPlayer, so the museum offers little to borrow. Part 09 of the first 3D game is the better model.

capabilities.use: Plays an imported character's clips and uses an AnimationTree blend space.
capabilities.understand: Skeleton3D, bones, retargeting, state machines, root motion.
capabilities.change: Builds a locomotion state machine and adds IK with a SkeletonModifier3D.
capabilities.caution: [M] AnimationTree appears in 6 files, Skeleton3D in 53. get_bone_global_pose() ignores SkeletonModifier3D; read bones through a BoneAttachment3D created in _ready.

capabilities.use: Plays an imported .wav or .ogg with AudioStreamPlayer or AudioStreamPlayer3D when something happens.
capabilities.understand: 2D vs 3D players; attenuation; buses; volume in dB; loop flags set on import; polyphony.
capabilities.change: Builds a bus/effects mix and a volume setting, and syncs to music.
capabilities.caution: [M] The SoundBank autoload exists, the default bus layout is set by uid, and audio input (microphone) is enabled. [M] A camera that takes over also takes the audio listener (project memory).

capabilities.use: Pushes frames into an AudioStreamGenerator's playback from _process.
capabilities.understand: Sample rate, buffer length, continuous phase, and audio timing vs frame timing.
capabilities.change: Writes a synth voice and moves the work off the main thread safely.
capabilities.caution: [M] 45 files (the Wavefunctions and WCN halls). FMPianoSynth's WorkerThreadPool tasks crashed Godot at exit until every task id was waited.

capabilities.use: Converts a material to a ShaderMaterial, edits its uniforms, and writes a fragment that uses TIME and UV.
capabilities.understand: vertex vs fragment; built-ins; uniforms and hints; model, world and view space; render_mode.
capabilities.change: Writes displacement, triplanar and dissolve shaders, knowing that moving vertices does not move collision.
capabilities.caution: [M] There are 304 .gdshader files. PI, TAU and E are built in, and redefining one is a SHADER ERROR that check_compile.gd cannot see and headless never shows. The Android preset has shader_baker disabled [I: shaders may stutter as they compile on first sight on Quest]. The shaders halls have no tutorial.md.

capabilities.use: Writes a sky shader, a canvas_item shader for UI, or a particle process shader.
capabilities.understand: Each shader_type's built-ins and when it runs.
capabilities.change: Makes a custom sky or post-processing.
capabilities.caution: [M] 18 canvas_item, 4 sky and 1 particles shader. In a sky shader, LIGHT0_DIRECTION points AT the light.

capabilities.use: Renders a SubViewport into a ViewportTexture used by a material.
capabilities.understand: Render targets, update modes, ping-pong feedback, reading the screen and depth textures.
capabilities.change: Builds GPU reaction-diffusion or trails.
capabilities.caution: [M] 31 files read the screen or depth texture. Per project memory, the reaction-diffusion (RD) buffer in the shaders sequence is still an open problem. [K] Stereo rendering multiplies this cost on Quest.

capabilities.use: Uses GPUParticles3D with a ParticleProcessMaterial and a draw-pass mesh, including a one-shot burst.
capabilities.understand: Emission shapes, amount and lifetime, local vs world coordinates, the visibility AABB, GPU vs CPU particles.
capabilities.change: Adds sub-emitters, trails, attractors, collision and custom process shaders.
capabilities.caution: [M] 111 GPUParticles3D vs 11 CPUParticles3D; env.gd sets particle visibility ranges for mobile_vr. [D] GPU particle collision does not work under Compatibility. [I] Particles cannot be judged in headless probes. The critique flags particles as missing from the proposal.

capabilities.use: Bakes a NavigationRegion3D and sends a NavigationAgent3D to a target.
capabilities.understand: Bake parameters vs agent size; path queries; avoidance; AStar3D for routing on a graph.
capabilities.change: Rebakes at runtime and runs A* on its own data.
capabilities.caution: [M] Only 11 files use Navigation*3D and 3 use AStar. Ada's routing is its own offline Python grid pathfinder (tools/map_pathfinder.py), so the engine side must be opened fresh in Graph Theory or Procedural Generation.

capabilities.use: Uses randf() and randi_range(), and a RandomNumberGenerator with a seed.
capabilities.understand: Seed plus state fix the sequence; draw order matters; global vs local RNG; weighted choices.
capabilities.change: Makes generation reproducible from a saved seed or state, and shuffles without replacement.
capabilities.caution: [M] 597 files. An unseeded randf once made five DNA variants into five unrelated objects; the fix was seed exports plus dna.fixture. [K] The same seed does not give the same physics outcome at a different physics rate or on another device.

capabilities.use: Samples FastNoiseLite with get_noise_2d/3d, and puts a NoiseTexture2D on a material.
capabilities.understand: Frequency, fractal octaves, seed, domain warp, the choice of sampling coordinates.
capabilities.change: Builds terrain or fields with chunked sampling.
capabilities.caution: [M] 167 files. A NoiseTexture2D generates its first image on the main thread, which cost the museum 5.1 s per boot; assign the noise with set_deferred.

capabilities.use: Writes with FileAccess.open('user://...', WRITE) and JSON.stringify, and reads back with JSON.parse_string.
capabilities.understand: res:// is read-only in an export, unlike user://; JSON loses types (Vector3, int); ConfigFile for settings; store_var for binary.
capabilities.change: Designs a versioned save schema with migration and error handling.
capabilities.caution: [M] FileAccess is in 879 files and JSON in 735, but ConfigFile in only 4. On the Quest, VR feedback lands in user:// and needs tools/pull_vr_feedback.py to come back. Exports exclude ada_run/**, so runtime data has to be copied into commons/data.

capabilities.use: Uses UndoRedo: create_action, add_do_method, add_undo_method, commit_action.
capabilities.understand: Commands vs snapshots; merge modes; history limits.
capabilities.change: Builds undo for an in-game editor, and versioned saves.
capabilities.caution: [M] No file uses UndoRedo, so there is nothing in the project to borrow. Post-Foundations would introduce it from scratch.

capabilities.use: Reads the Debugger monitors (FPS, draw calls, objects) and runs the Profiler.
capabilities.understand: Frame time vs FPS; CPU-bound vs GPU-bound; per-function cost; physics time.
capabilities.change: Times its own code with Time.get_ticks_usec, sets budgets, and profiles on the target device.
capabilities.caution: [M] A cellular-automaton (BaseCA) work whose picture has settled still costs 15–76 ms a frame on desktop, so time each work's own _process. Profile on the Quest (Mobile renderer, about an 11–14 ms budget at 72–90 Hz [K]), not only on desktop Forward+.

capabilities.use: Uses WorkerThreadPool.add_task with wait_for_task_completion, and ResourceLoader.load_threaded_request.
capabilities.understand: Only thread-safe APIs may run off the main thread; never touch the active scene tree from a thread; hand results back with call_deferred.
capabilities.change: Moves a generator's data work to a thread and publishes the result on the main thread.
capabilities.caution: [M] Every task id must be waited, or Godot crashes at exit. A threaded load on Quest raced class_name registration. Only 1 file outside addons uses WorkerThreadPool.

capabilities.use: Spreads a loop over frames with await get_tree().process_frame, and uses visibility ranges and LOD.
capabilities.understand: In XR a dropped frame means discomfort; chunking; dirty flags; occlusion.
capabilities.change: Builds a generator time-sliced to a per-frame millisecond budget, with streaming.
capabilities.caution: [M] The museum keeps only 2 segments of halls live at a time, and env.gd sets scaling_3d_scale to 0.8 on mobile_vr. [I] Add these techniques only against a problem you have measured, as the proposal says.

capabilities.use: Adds @tool so a script previews in the editor.
capabilities.understand: Engine.is_editor_hint(); tool code runs on open scenes and can save data into them; EditorPlugin and inspector plugins.
capabilities.change: Writes a dock or a custom inspector for its own data.
capabilities.caution: [M] 214 files use @tool, and addons hold 14 EditorPlugin scripts (map_tool_3d and others). Much of Ada's tooling lives outside Godot (Python tools, the encyclopedia's web editors); teach that boundary. [K] A buggy tool setter can save wrong values into scenes.

capabilities.use: Runs a script with godot --headless --script that asserts and exits with a status code.
capabilities.understand: What headless cannot see (drawn frames, MultiMesh data, shader errors, GPU readback); predicting before measuring; negative tests.
capabilities.change: Builds a check harness or CI, or adopts GUT/gdUnit4 (community tools, not built in).
capabilities.caution: [M] commons/testing holds 931 scripts (515 probes), tools/ holds 830 Python scripts, and there is check_compile.gd and a 16-second watchdog; no test addon is installed. Recorded traps: emitting a signal is not input; a comparison needs a readback.

capabilities.use: Enables OpenXR and XR shaders, adds XROrigin3D, XRCamera3D and two XRController3D, and writes a start script (use_xr, vsync off).
capabilities.understand: Tracking space and origin, refresh rate, the action map, and the renderer choice for standalone headsets.
capabilities.change: Configures action maps, refresh rate, passthrough, and foveation/VRS.
capabilities.caution: [D] The docs recommend Compatibility for standalone headsets, yet the Quest build runs Mobile [M], and foveation_level=3 only acts under Compatibility, with no vrs_mode set anywhere [M]. [I] Foveation is probably inert on the Quest. This is core for Ada but a branch for a general 3D developer.

capabilities.use: Uses XR Tools: FunctionPickup with XRToolsPickable, FunctionPointer, MovementDirect/Turn, PlayerBody.
capabilities.understand: What OpenXR provides vs what XR Tools adds; pickable layers; hand poses; comfort options.
capabilities.change: Writes a custom movement provider or pickable, with desktop equivalents.
capabilities.caution: [M] XR Tools 4.5.1 is untracked in git, and 307 files reference XRTools* classes. vr_staging's movement_only_hands once stripped grab from all of VR. The headset runs an export, so debug from the Quest log, not from desktop parity.

capabilities.use: Installs export templates, adds a preset, exports a build and runs it outside the editor.
capabilities.understand: What goes into the .pck; include and exclude filters; res:// is read-only; feature tags; debug vs release.
capabilities.change: Sets up an Android/Quest gradle build, signing and per-platform overrides.
capabilities.caution: [M] Only Android and Web presets exist, with no Windows one, so the 'export something small early' step needs a desktop preset added. The android/ template is gitignored. A running editor deploys with the preset it loaded at startup; edits to export_presets.cfg need a restart.

capabilities.use: Drops a .glb, .png or .ogg into the FileSystem, instances the model, and reimports after changing settings.
capabilities.understand: The Import dock and .import sidecar files; a glTF's scale, origin and materials; extracting materials; licences.
capabilities.change: Uses import presets, post-import scripts and inherited scenes.
capabilities.caution: [M] Blender import is disabled and /assets/ is gitignored. Ada is almost entirely procedural, so an import workshop must bring its own asset. [D] The first 3D game imports a .glb in part 02.

capabilities.use: Uses Node2D, Sprite2D, CharacterBody2D, Camera2D and TileMapLayer.
capabilities.understand: 2D coordinates (y points down); 2D physics is separate from 3D.
capabilities.change: Translates a 3D study (trace, grid, cellular automaton) into 2D.
capabilities.caution: [M] Only 29 files use 2D nodes. [D] Godot's own path puts the 2D game before 3D; Ada reverses that, so treat 2D as a parallel branch.

capabilities.use: Hosts and joins with ENetMultiplayerPeer, and uses MultiplayerSpawner/Synchronizer and @rpc.
capabilities.understand: Authority, latency, and what needs replicating.
capabilities.change: Builds a two-person room.
capabilities.caution: [M] No file uses networking, so there is nothing to borrow. As the proposal says, a shared room would be a new tested deliverable.

capabilities.use: Playtests its own scene: shows an instruction, gives a response to an action, and offers a retry.
capabilities.understand: Invitation, action, feedback, then retry or leave; testing with another person.
capabilities.change: Redesigns the invitation and the feedback based on observed play.
capabilities.caution: [K] Godot has no documentation on game design; score-and-replay is its only loop lesson. [M] Ada's equivalents: pipeline stage 6 (VR testing), the ada_run/desktop_feedback.md bridge, and the rule that 'pathfinder OK' is not evidence a hall can be walked.

capabilities.use: Provides subtitles or text alternatives, volume and mute, and readable font sizes.
capabilities.understand: Remappable input; XR comfort (snap vs smooth turn, vignette, seated play); controller focus navigation.
capabilities.change: Builds a settings screen that saves and applies, and adds text-to-speech.
capabilities.caution: [M] The Subtitles and SceneNarrator autoloads exist, and XRToolsUserSettings holds comfort settings [K]. Check Label3D legibility at distance in the headset.

capabilities.use: Finds which renderer each platform actually uses (Project Settings > Rendering > Renderer, including rendering_method.mobile).
capabilities.understand: The Forward+/Mobile/Compatibility feature table (fog, SSR, SSAO, SDFGI, decals, compute) and the XR recommendations.
capabilities.change: Sets the renderer per platform and designs looks that survive on the target renderer.
capabilities.caution: [M] rendering_method is unset (Forward+ on desktop, Mobile on Quest [K]), while [D] the docs recommend Compatibility for Quest. A learner who judges on desktop Forward+ will not see what the headset shows. See light.env and xr.setup.

capabilities.use: Pauses with get_tree().paused = true and a menu set to When Paused.
capabilities.understand: process_mode (Inherit, Pausable, WhenPaused, Always, Disabled); what stops while paused; signals still fire.
capabilities.change: Pauses one subsystem locally vs the whole game.
capabilities.caution: [M] 41 files set paused or process_mode, and the DeathEffect autoload freezes time. [D] Animations, audio and particles pause automatically. The critique's test is that the resume button must still work while paused.

capabilities.use: Places or moves things along a Path3D with PathFollow3D.progress_ratio.
capabilities.understand: Curve3D points and handles, baked length, tilt.
capabilities.change: Generates a curve from a recorded trace.
capabilities.caution: [M] 17 files. The proposal names Curve3D as a later use of Point_Trace's recorded path.
